title: BCSR on GPU: A Way Forward Extreme-scale Graph Processing on Accelerator-enabled Frontier Supercomputer
problem: 2D partitioned graph processing creates sparse local graphs where CSR format wastes significant memory, with >83% of vertices having empty edges. Memory-efficient sparse data structures are critical for distributed graph processing on large-scale systems.
motivation: Efficient memory representation of sparse graphs is essential for scaling graph analytics on GPU-accelerated supercomputers like Frontier.
method: BCSR (bit-CSR) is a modified CSR representation that uses bitwise operations to compress sparse graph structures more efficiently than standard CSR. The approach encodes sparse vertices with empty edges using bit-level compression, reducing memory footprint on GPUs while maintaining computational efficiency. Performance is evaluated on the Graph500 benchmark using sparse rmat datasets with hundreds of millions of vertices and edges.
key_novelty: Application of bit-level compression to CSR format for reducing memory waste in sparse graph representations on GPU architectures.
contributions: Proposed BCSR format for memory-efficient representation of sparse graphs on GPUs
Demonstrated 16.67% memory savings on sparse rmat dataset without performance degradation
Achieved 33% theoretical and experimental storage reduction for graphs with >83% sparse vertices
Analysis of BCSR performance on GPU-accelerated Frontier supercomputer for Graph500 benchmark

metrics.other: 16.67% memory savings on sparse rmat dataset, 33% theoretical storage reduction

limitations: 1.7× slowdown in degree lookup times due to bitwise operations reveals performance trade-offs that may limit practical adoption in latency-sensitive scenarios.
primary_theme: Sparse graph memory compression for GPU acceleration
